data.name: Og
data.gender_notes: Og is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In biblical texts, Og is described as a giant or a strong leader. The name may have derived from the Hebrew word 'og' meaning 'giant' or 'monster'. In Numbers 21:33-35, Og is mentioned as the last king of Bashan, whose bed was a bedstead of iron. The name Og carries the meaning “Giant or Strong” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Og usually hope their child will grow to embody giant or strong and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength and power, both in physical and spiritual senses.
data.etymology: Og belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Giant or Strong.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Og total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: עוֹג
in_hebrew.meaning: שם מלך עמון שהיה גדול ומפורסם
in_hebrew.long_meaning: במקרא, עוֹג (עברית: עוֹג) היה נסיך עמון, חברו של רב־עמל, ושליט יששכר. עוֹג נזכר בספר במדבר (21:13–24) כמלך עמון. שם עוֹג נזכר גם במקור עברי לאדם גדול, או לדבר גדול.

in_greek.name: Ωγ
in_greek.meaning: βασιλιάς των Αμωνούς, μεγάλος και φαμαρκός
in_greek.long_meaning: Στην Βίβλο, Ωγ (Ελληνικά: Ωγ) ήταν βασιλιάς των Αμωνούς. Ένας από τους μεγαλύτερους βασιλείς στην lịchη Βίβλο. Ο Ωγ είναι ένα από τα πιο γνωστά ονόματα στους Βιβλικούς αιώνες.

in_latin.name: Og
in_latin.long_meaning: In Biblia, Og (Latin: Og) fuit rex Moaborum, unus magnorum regum in antiqua historia. Nomen Og a fontibus Hebraeo-Graecis originem ducit, et significat regem magni et famosi.

in_english.name: Og
in_english.meaning: king of the Ammonites, great and famous
in_english.long_meaning: In the Bible, Og (English: Og) was the king of the Ammonites, one of the greatest kings in ancient history. The name Og originates from the Hebrew and Greek roots, and it means a great and famous king.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Og" carries a rich cultural significance, with its roots tracing back to the Old Testament. Throughout history, the name "Og" has been associated with strength, power, and leadership. The name's linkage to giants in biblical texts has fostered a sense of awe and reverence in various Christian communities.
data.spiritual_significance: spiritually, the name "Og" can serve as a reminder of God's power and might. The Hebrew origin of the name underscores the theme of God's ability to overcome seemingly insurmountable challenges. Additionally, the historical significance of Og as a powerful and influential leader encourages reflection on leadership in Christian life and the importance of being a strong and faith-filled leader.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Og: The strong and enduring one. Rooted in the Old Testament figure Og, a king of Bashan known for his size and strength. In Christianity, Og symbolizes the unwavering faith and resilience against adversity.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Og remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.
